pearls.blurb: Collect a still cube. Add rising, turning and swelling to its moving demonstrations, then walk a ramp to the completed pickups.
pearls.speak: Observe the still cube before collecting it; three moving demonstrations remain. Add translation, rotation and scale, then climb to four finished pickups.

says.pick_up_cube: The first cube holds still. Pause before approaching and watch a corner: nothing shifts. Then walk into it: even without an animation, it can be collected. Keep its shape in mind as you go to the next one.

pearls.blurb: Cross by translation, scale and rotation; then slide the far bank while the plank keeps its original motion. Which part of the crossing did the background supply?
pearls.speak: Compare translation, scaling and rotation as crossings, without the head crab. Move the far bank while the plank keeps its motion: what makes the crossing possible?

says.tc: A cube travels between the banks. Let it make a journey without you. Its top meets the floor at each end; between them, it is a small piece of floor with nothing beside it.
says.sc: At the next gap, the green cube stays in one place. Watch its upper face. It rises as the cube grows; its edges approach the banks.
says.rc: The third gap has a thin orange plank. Wait through a turn before stepping onto it. Across the lane, it reaches towards the sides. After a quarter-turn, its long dimension reaches along your route.
says.adjustable_landing: Before leaving, take the side aisle to the small control marked MOVE THE BANK. The far landing rests on rails. Slide BANK a little, then watch the orange plank make its usual turn.

pearls.blurb: Seven journeys separate and combine x, y and z. At the exit, two hand-operated mechanisms share a destination but permit different paths.
pearls.speak: Thirteen pickups sit on seven carrier routes through x, y and z. Two exit mechanisms share a destination but permit different journeys; the turning torus anticipates rotation.

says.tc: The first carrier travels into depth. Step aboard and let the room pass. Look at the cube under your feet: it keeps its facing and size. Along this journey, only its z coordinate changes.
says.pick_up_cube: The small pickups have been waiting along these journeys. They rise and fall without turning. Their small vertical loop continues as the carrier brings you into contact with them, and each collected cube disappears with a sound.
says.translation_cube_demo: Step onto the final terrace. Two small door mechanisms wait at hand height. Their handles have the same distance to travel upwards and sideways. Try taking the diagonal.

pearls.blurb: Cross a level Y bridge; ride an upright end-platform forward around X or sideways around Z. Compare two body widths in the rotated arrays, then enter the tunnel and repeated cake profiles.

pearls.blurb: Position, orientation and size follow clocks. Read the moving obstacles and find when your body can pass.
pearls.speak: Timed pushers, rotating slabs and synchronised growers change access on level ground. At the exit, two armoured door leaves combine translation, rotation and scale into a passage that opens on approach.

says.pusher_block: Three red blocks, each with an arrow on its face. Follow one through a complete journey before entering its path. It travels, stops, returns and stops again. The pause is part of the movement you need to learn.

transformation.blurb: Collect a still cube. Add rising, turning and swelling to its moving demonstrations, then walk a ramp to the completed pickups.
transformation.speak: Observe the still cube before collecting it; three moving demonstrations remain. Add translation, rotation and scale, then climb to four finished pickups.

says.pick_up_cube: The first cube holds still. Pause before approaching and watch a corner: nothing shifts. Then walk into it: even without an animation, it can be collected. Keep its shape in mind as you go to the next one.

transformation.blurb: Cross by translation, scale and rotation; then slide the far bank while the plank keeps its original motion. Which part of the crossing did the background supply?
transformation.speak: Compare translation, scaling and rotation as crossings, without the head crab. Move the far bank while the plank keeps its motion: what makes the crossing possible?

says.tc: A cube travels between the banks. Let it make a journey without you. Its top meets the floor at each end; between them, it is a small piece of floor with nothing beside it.
says.sc: At the next gap, the green cube stays in one place. Watch its upper face. It rises as the cube grows; its edges approach the banks.
says.rc: The third gap has a thin orange plank. Wait through a turn before stepping onto it. Across the lane, it reaches towards the sides. After a quarter-turn, its long dimension reaches along your route.
says.adjustable_landing: Before leaving, take the side aisle to the small control marked MOVE THE BANK. The far landing rests on rails. Slide BANK a little, then watch the orange plank make its usual turn.

transformation.blurb: Seven journeys separate and combine x, y and z. At the exit, two hand-operated mechanisms share a destination but permit different paths.
transformation.speak: Thirteen pickups sit on seven carrier routes through x, y and z. Two exit mechanisms share a destination but permit different journeys; the turning torus anticipates rotation.

says.tc: The first carrier travels into depth. Step aboard and let the room pass. Look at the cube under your feet: it keeps its facing and size. Along this journey, only its z coordinate changes.
says.pick_up_cube: The small pickups have been waiting along these journeys. They rise and fall without turning. Their small vertical loop continues as the carrier brings you into contact with them, and each collected cube disappears with a sound.
says.translation_cube_demo: Step onto the final terrace. Two small door mechanisms wait at hand height. Their handles have the same distance to travel upwards and sideways. Try taking the diagonal.

transformation.blurb: Cross a level Y bridge; ride an upright end-platform forward around X or sideways around Z. Compare two body widths in the rotated arrays, then enter the tunnel and repeated cake profiles.
transformation.speak: Compare a level Y bridge and upright X/Z rides, two body widths in rotated arrays, a tunnel and five carousel profiles. Which dimensions make space for this body?

says.rotation_wall_crossings: The green blade turns around y. Its centre stays over the gap while its ends sweep towards the grid. At ninety degrees it pauses. Walk across the length that has arrived in your direction of travel.
says.rotation_array_compare: Four bands each contain two columns and six rows of cubes. Begin at zero. Choose a column and walk forward along z.
says.boolean_tunnel: Look through the first hollow cube. Four more stand beyond it. Walk inside and follow a corner with your eye.
says.carousel_cake: Step out beside the turning stacks. Follow a stripe on a low layer, then near the top. Stand still. Their relations keep changing.

transformation.blurb: A four-metre room grows fourfold. The body keeps its size; descend the serving tower and compare a growing doorway with a fixed museum frame.
transformation.speak: Take the bottle: the room changes to four times its size in one update, then your body is relocated onto the table. Descend and compare the enlarged doorway with a fixed museum frame.

says.scale_me: In the rotation hall, you tried the openings against the size of your body. Here, something waits to be taken.

transformation.blurb: Approach turns slats, contact removes cells, proximity shrinks blocks. Two openings close behind you; one records your passage.
transformation.speak: Approach turns slats and shrinks blocks; contact cuts an open-topped trench in a low lattice. Step clear to see reversible openings return; the cut remains.

says.approach_wall: A wall of upright slats stands across the way. There is no handle, no plate, no light that turns green. Walk at it.
says.carve_grid: The next throat holds a low block of small cubes, about 1.3 metres high. You can look over it. The lattice reaches across the way, but it does not enclose your head.
says.approach_scale: Nine blocks, set closer together than a pair of shoulders. At rest the gap between neighbours is thirty-five centimetres, which is not "tight". It is shut.

transformation.blurb: Position, orientation and size follow clocks. Read the moving obstacles and find when your body can pass.
transformation.speak: Timed pushers, rotating slabs and synchronised growers change access on level ground. At the exit, two armoured door leaves combine translation, rotation and scale into a passage that opens on approach.

says.pusher_block: Three red blocks, each with an arrow on its face. Follow one through a complete journey before entering its path. It travels, stops, returns and stops again. The pause is part of the movement you need to learn.
says.rc: The middle room has two orange turning slabs. Watch one end while the centre stays put. It takes two seconds to make a quarter-turn, waits, then reverses. One slab pauses for four seconds; the other for three.
says.grower_block: The last room has three cubes sharing a tempo. Wait before approaching. They grow anyway. Watch them together first; the repetition makes the size change easier to read.
says.transformation_airlock: After the growing cubes, two armoured leaves meet inside a heavy frame. Approach, then stop. Follow the bright strip along one leaf.
